item.title: Suno Releases v6 AI Music Model with Record Industry Support
item.description:
Suno Releases v6 AI Music Model with Record Industry Support

Suno has launched v6, its first AI music model developed with support from the record industry. The model is being rolled out starting today, and Suno intends to eventually retire its previous models.

🧩 How it works

According to Suno’s Jack Brody, v6 was “trained from the ground up, with a new set of data that does not include the same data that our previous models were trained on.”

Training data includes:

  • Content licensed from partners Believe, BMG, and Warner Music Group
  • “User data”

It remains unclear if the training data is completely free of dubiously obtained content.

⚙️ Key details

Suno v6 consists of three different models:

Model Description
v6-mini Available for free to all; focused on fast, resource-light creation. Results are simpler and often contain more artifacts.
v6-wild Designed for “happy accidents and natural imperfections.”
v6 The standard model.

Capabilities and Performance

  • Genre Understanding: All three models show dramatic improvement in understanding genres, accurately capturing the superficial hallmarks of styles such as “krautrock” or “hyperpop.”
  • Multimodal Prompts: Users are no longer limited to text; v6 can create tracks based on video, images, or other audio.
  • Editing and Mashups: Users can now use plain language within a chat to edit specific parts of a song, such as a single lyric or guitar line, without regenerating the entire track. The model can also combine multiple elements from a user’s Suno library into new creations.

Limitations

  • Human Imperfections: The model cannot capture “natural imperfections.” Attempts to produce dissonant, off-key, or out-of-tune results—including “out-of-tune piano played haphazardly”—have failed.
  • Prompt Adherence: v6 may ignore specific prompts, such as requests for “no drums” or “monotone vocals.”
  • AI Artifacts: Vocals in v6 may produce more harsh-edged artifacts common to AI models than those found in v5.

🚀 Availability

Suno v6 starts rolling out today.

#Suno #AImusic #GenerativeAI #MusicIndustry

Source: Suno releases its first AI music model made with record industry help

item.title: ARIA bans fully AI-generated songs from official Australian music charts
item.description:
ARIA bans fully AI-generated songs from official Australian music charts

Australia’s official chart body, ARIA, has changed its rules so that recordings created primarily by artificial intelligence are no longer eligible to appear on the ARIA Charts.

🔍 Overview

  • AI‑generated music has pushed the music industry into new territory.
  • While many countries are introducing copyright, transparency and labeling rules, ARIA has taken the most explicit step by drawing a clear line for chart eligibility.

⚙️ Rule specifics

  • The restriction applies when AI is responsible for the main creative performance of a track.
  • Examples of ineligible recordings:
    • A song with an AI‑generated lead vocal.
    • A track where a major instrumental performance is generated by AI.
    • Recordings created almost entirely from AI prompts.
  • AI can still be used for supporting tools such as mastering, stem separation, or other production assistance.
  • The rule does not prevent artists from using AI at all; it only bars fully AI‑created works from chart competition.

🌍 Global context

  • Europe has introduced transparency requirements for AI‑generated content.
  • The UK is discussing copyright and AI training, and the US is moving to protect artists’ voices and identities.
  • Music organisations are adding clearer labeling for AI recordings and setting new chart‑qualification conditions.
  • Spotify plans to display AI Persona badges on artist profiles built around AI identities.
  • Data company Luminate has launched a framework within its CONNECT platform to identify AI‑generated songs and artist profiles, reporting thousands of such recordings already in its database.
  • These initiatives show the industry is shifting from treating AI music as a side note to actively tracking and measuring it.

📊 Impact

  • Despite new rules elsewhere, AI‑generated tracks can still appear on many official charts.
  • ARIA’s rule is currently the clearest line, ensuring that only music with a primary human creative performance competes on its charts.
  • The change may influence other markets to adopt similar eligibility standards.

#AIMusic #MusicIndustry #ARIA #Copyright

Source: AUSTRALIA BECOMES FIRST COUNTRY TO BAN FULLY AI-GENERATED MUSIC FROM OFFICIAL CHARTS - AStepFWD

item.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic Over Copyrighted Works
item.description:
Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic Over Copyrighted Works

Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed a lawsuit against AI company Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, alleging unauthorized use of copyrighted materials. The publishers characterize the incident as one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history.

⚙️ Key details

  • The suit seeks damages for tens of thousands of copyrighted works.
  • Plaintiffs are asking for up to $150,000 per work, plus up to $25,000 for each instance where copyright data was allegedly stripped.
  • Total potential damages could reach several billion dollars if the court awards the maximum amount.
  • The complaint names Anthropic as an entity, along with co-founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann as individual defendants.

🧩 Allegations

  • The suit claims Benjamin Mann used BitTorrent to download over five million pirated books.
  • Anthropic employees are alleged to have downloaded at least two million more books from the Pirate Library Mirror.
  • The company is accused of scraping lyrics from licensed platforms like MusixMatch and LyricFind.
  • The complaint alleges these actions were taken to develop and operate the “Claude” series of AI models.

🎼 Sampled Works

The following songs were cited in the suit as examples of content found within Anthropic’s training data:

Song Title Artist
Ain’t No Mountain High Enough Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell
Livin’ On a Prayer Bon Jovi
September Earth, Wind & Fire
Hallelujah Leonard Cohen
Paper Rings Taylor Swift

*Update August 30th: Clarification has been added that Sony Music Publishing specifically filed suit, not to be confused with Sony Music Entertainment.

#Anthropic #Copyright #Lawsuit #Claude #MusicIndustry

Source: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
